rule: The Eastern-Central boundary in Kentucky (49 CFR 71.5(c)) runs from the Indiana line along the west lines of Meade and Hardin counties, the south lines of Hardin and Larue counties, around Taylor County, along the west and south lines of Casey and Pulaski counties and the west line of Wayne County to Tennessee; the forty-one counties listed lie wholly west of it, in the Central zone. The rest of the state keeps Eastern time.
